process_area.title: Outbound Plastic Recovery Partnerships & Waste-to-Energy Co-Processing

value_stream.name: Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) Compliance & Plastic Recovery Network

fields.Participants: Stock Associates (VS-07), Store Staff, Cleaning Service (VS-98)
fields.Trigger: Store daily operations; store cleanup routines (VS-07)
fields.Volume: 200 stores collecting ~2–3 metric tons of plastic waste monthly

workflows.name: Retail Store In-Store Plastic Waste Sorting, Collection & Storage

Automation Opportunity: - Digital scale weight logging with barcode tagging.
Controls: - CTL-768 (ensure controlled execution — Outbound Plastic Recovery Partnerships & Waste-to-Energy Co-Processing (PA-179.2).)
- CTL-768: Weekly safety inspection checks storage zones; store weight logs verified by Regional LP (VS-23).
Cross-references: - links to VS-07 (store ops), VS-23 (loss prevention), VS-98 (contingent workforce), VS-24 (HSE)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fire Hazard**: Stored plastics ignite in the receiving backroom; mitigated by store fire safety standards (sprinkler coverage, clearance zones) per VS-24.2.
System Touchpoints: - Store operations logs (VS-07), Safety checklists (VS-24), Security system (VS-23).

steps.activity: Set up clearly labeled Customer Recycling Bins at checkout areas and customer service counters.
Sort packaging waste in receiving area: separate clean LDPE stretch wrap, bubble wrap, plastic bands, and PET containers generated during receiving operations.
Compact and bale sorted plastics using store compaction equipment; label bales with store ID, weight, and date.
Stage compacted plastic bales in designated dry storage zones to prevent moisture and fire hazards (VS-24).

fields.Owner: EPR Regional Coordinator / Government Affairs Manager (VS-104)
fields.Participants: LGU Solid Waste Management Board, Barangay Captains, CSR team (VS-152)
fields.Trigger: LGU partnership initiative; regional EPR program expansion
fields.Volume: ~40–50 LGU partnerships active across six regions

workflows.name: LGU/MRF (Materials Recovery Facility) Plastic Waste Recovery Collaboration

Automation Opportunity: - Weight logging on mobile app at LGU sites.
Controls: - CTL-768: MOA approved by Legal and LGU Council; monthly weight receipts verified by LGU Treasurer.
Cross-references: - links to VS-104 (government affairs), VS-152 (CSR), VS-06 (logistics), VS-76 (LGU compliance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Dirty / Unusable plastic supply**: LGU plastics contaminated with organic waste, causing partner rejection; mitigated by LGU worker sorting training program.
System Touchpoints: - Government affairs CRM (VS-104), CSR project system (VS-152), ERP Logistics module (VS-06).

steps.activity: Identify target municipalities with active Materials Recovery Facilities (MRFs).

steps.activity: Draft MOA for Plastic Waste Sorting & Supply: BuildRight provides sorting equipment, waste bins, or LGU funding in exchange for clean segregated consumer plastics collected by LGU sweepers.

fields.Participants: Junk Shop Owners, Waste Collectors, Finance (VS-17.4), CSR Foundation (VS-152)
fields.Volume: ~150–200 registered informal waste collectors / junk shops

workflows.name: Junk Shop & Informal Waste Collector Network Registration & Incentivization

Automation Opportunity: - Mobile wallet payments (GCash/Maya) to informal collectors.
Controls: - CTL-768: Weighing certified on calibrated scales; payout receipts require dual cashier sign-off.
Cross-references: - links to VS-115 (calibration), VS-169 (PPE), VS-17.4 (FP&A), VS-152 (CSR), VS-03.4 (vendor portal), VS-15 (P2P)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cash management fraud**: Paying premiums for non-plastic waste or double-counting; mitigated by strict scale audits (VS-115) and cashier controls.
System Touchpoints: - Supplier portal (VS-03.4), scale database (VS-115), AP cash payout (VS-15).

steps.activity: Register local junk shops and informal collector cooperatives in BuildRight's EPR partner network.
Provide weighing scales (VS-115) and protective equipment (PPE - VS-169) to registered informal collectors.
Establish the BuildRight Plastic Buying Premium: pay a cash premium above local market rates for targeted plastics delivered to BuildRight stores/DCs.
Reconcile delivered weights, issue payment receipts, and record collectors' livelihood metrics (VS-152).

fields.Participants: Fleet Drivers, DC Receiving Team (VS-04), 3PL Logistics Partner (VS-56)
fields.Volume: ~60–80 metric tons consolidated monthly across 4 DCs

workflows.name: Logistics Consolidation, Baling & Transport of Recovered Plastics to DCs

Automation Opportunity: - Fleet tracking and routing algorithms for backhaul optimization.
Controls: - CTL-768: DC scale verification against store dispatch weights; variances over 5% investigated.
Cross-references: - links to VS-04 (DC ops), VS-06 (logistics), VS-56 (3PL), VS-110 (freight procurement)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Inbound route delay**: Empty backhauls delayed by heavy traffic, blocking store docks; mitigated by scheduling pickups during low-traffic periods.
System Touchpoints: - WMS (VS-04), Fleet management system (VS-06), carrier booking portal (VS-56).

steps.activity: Configure route schedule: request empty backhaul fleet trucks returning from store deliveries (VS-06) to pick up compacted plastic bales at stores.
Log weight at store loading bay before truck loading.
Unload and consolidate plastic bales at regional DCs in the dedicated EPR storage yard.
Bale loose LGU/junk shop plastics at the DC bale facility; arrange full truckload transfers to final co-processing/recycling plants.

workflows.name: Cement Kiln Co-Processing Partnership Agreement & Recovery Logistics

Automation Opportunity: - Electronic delivery confirmation matching between systems.
Controls: - CTL-768 (ensure controlled execution — Outbound Plastic Recovery Partnerships & Waste-to-Energy Co-Processing (PA-179.2).)
- CTL-768: Co-processing agreements reviewed by Legal; deliveries recorded against cement purchase offsets.
Cross-references: - links to VS-03 (procurement), VS-04 (DC ops), VS-06 (logistics), VS-100 (legal)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Plant rejects shipment**: Contaminated plastics rejected at plant gate, causing demurrage; mitigated by strict DC pre-inspection and bale moisture checks.
System Touchpoints: - ERP Procurement (VS-03), WMS dispatch (VS-04), transport dispatch (VS-06).

fields.Participants: Recycling Plant Owners, WMS Team (VS-04), Quality (VS-31)
fields.Trigger: EPR plastic portfolio diversification; clean PET/HDPE recovery volume growth

workflows.name: Mechanical Recycling Partner Onboarding, Sourcing & Recovery Logistics

Controls: - CTL-768 (ensure controlled execution — Outbound Plastic Recovery Partnerships & Waste-to-Energy Co-Processing (PA-179.2).)
- CTL-768: Recycler accreditation certificates verified annually; weight logs checked by QA.
Cross-references: - links to VS-03 (procurement), VS-04 (DC ops), VS-31 (quality), VS-161 (third-party risk), VS-03.4 (vendor portal)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Partner default**: Recycler closed by DENR for water treatment violations; mitigated by annual environmental compliance checklist audits.
System Touchpoints: - Vendor portal (VS-03.4), WMS dispatch (VS-04), ERP invoicing (VS-15).

steps.activity: Onboard accredited local plastic recyclers: verify licenses, environmental compliance, and processing capacity.
Establish grade requirements: separate clear PET bottles, HDPE jugs, and clean film wrap.
Logistics execution: transport sorted plastic bales from DC to recycler.
Secure Recycler Weight Certificates and material processing logs.

fields.Participants: Recovery Partners (Cement plant/Recycler), External Auditor, Document Control (VS-88)

workflows.name: Waste-to-Energy (WTE) Co-processing Certification & Recovery Audit Trails

Automation Opportunity: - Digital matching of DC scale records to uploaded partner certificate.
Controls: - CTL-768 (ensure controlled execution — Outbound Plastic Recovery Partnerships & Waste-to-Energy Co-Processing (PA-179.2).)
- CTL-768: Audit trails checked monthly by internal audit; matching verified before payment release.
Cross-references: - links to VS-88 (document control), VS-21 (internal audit)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lost audit trail**: Missing weighbridge tickets invalidating recovery credits; mitigated by mandatory digital upload of documents at DC gate.
System Touchpoints: - Partner portal, Document control archive (VS-88), ERP asset system.

steps.activity: Request formal Co-Processing Certificates or Plastic Recovery Certificates (PRC) from partners for every delivered batch.
Verify certificates: cross-reference certificate weights against DC dispatch weight and carrier logs.
Compile the recovery audit trail folder: weighbridge tickets, delivery receipts, photos of processing, and signed certificates.
Upload compliance folders to the secure EPR compliance archive (VS-88).

fields.Participants: Store Managers, Logistics operators, DOLE Representative
fields.Trigger: EPR logistics / baling operations; DOLE OSH audit (VS-24)
fields.Volume: 4 DCs and 200 store collection zones monitored

workflows.name: Multi-Region Recovery Operations Safety & OSH Compliance

Automation Opportunity: - Baler safety sensor logs integration with central OSH dashboard.
Controls: - CTL-768 (ensure controlled execution — Outbound Plastic Recovery Partnerships & Waste-to-Energy Co-Processing (PA-179.2).)
- CTL-768: Baling machines inspected weekly; lock-out/tag-out keys managed by shift supervisors.
Cross-references: - links to VS-24 (HSE), VS-169 (PPE), VS-19.4 (HR training)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Laceration / Compaction injury**: Worker hand trapped in baler; mitigated by mandatory dual-button activation controls on all balers.
System Touchpoints: - OSH training logs, safety audit portal (VS-24), Employee training records (VS-19.4).

steps.activity: Establish Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for operating plastic baling and compaction machinery.
Train staff: run mandatory safety training on machine lock-out/tag-out, bale handling, and ergonomic lifting.
Enforce PPE compliance: require safety boots, heavy gloves, safety glasses, and ear protection around balers (VS-169).
Conduct quarterly fire risk assessments in dry plastic storage zones; verify fire extinguishers are serviced and clear.
